title: Market Run, Week 4
dek: Ollie Gordon II took 84 percent of Miami's snaps after Achane's ACL, and he is the first name on this week's list.
author: Chef Hazy
intro_md:
Updated Sat 12:25 PM ET: Keenan Allen is ruled out for London with the groin; the claim stands as a Week 5 flex.

Updated Fri 5:15 PM ET: Kenyon Sadiq is questionable and TE13 this week @CHI; the claim stands.

Updated Fri 5:00 PM ET: Jaylen Wright practiced in full and is listed as Miami's RB1, so he is the Miami back to roster at 5 to 10 percent and Ollie Gordon II drops to a 0 to 2 percent bench add; Terrance Ferguson is ruled out with Colby Parkinson questionable, so Tyler Higbee's stream depends on Parkinson; Keenan Allen and Kenyon Sadiq are questionable.

Updated Wed 3:45 PM ET: Tre' Harris moves from the adds to the stashes at 1 to 3 percent after his snap share fell to 58 percent with Ladd McConkey back full time; Ollie Gordon II's and Jaylen Wright's cards carry Wright's limited Wednesday practice.

Updated Wed 3:35 PM ET: Keenan Allen's card carries the league-discipline flag (three-game minimum under policy, nothing announced, court date Oct 26; the 3 to 6 percent claim stands), and Xavier Worthy's drop reason is corrected: he ran a 79 percent route share @MIA, the problem is 63 yards on 15 targets.

Week 3 broke three backfields. De'Von Achane is done for the year, Travis Etienne Jr. is out for Week 4 and longer, and Breece Hall is week to week. That puts the running backs at the top of the shop, with a rookie tight end right behind them.

FAAB ranges are percent of a 100 budget, written for 10 to 14 team leagues in full PPR. Rostered figures are from public waiver pages Tuesday morning; a blank means no clean number was available.
outro_md: The Menu lands Wednesday with every one of these players ranked. Claims first, lineups after.

adds.why: Gordon took 84 percent of Miami's snaps after Achane went down: 17 carries, 41 yards, a goal-line touchdown and 3 catches for 14 yards. Achane is on IR for the season. Jaylen Wright practiced in full Thursday, is expected to play at MIN and is listed first on the depth chart, with the staff signaling a shared workload, so Gordon is the second back in a split.
adds.verdict: Add him only as a bench back, 0 to 2 percent of FAAB. RB35 for me this week, a low-end RB3; sit him with Wright back.

adds.why: Travis Etienne Jr. re-aggravated his hamstring after 13 carries for 57 yards, and the Saints already ruled him out for Monday against ATL. After Etienne left, Kamara took 6 of the next 10 carries and 20 of the 34 second-half snaps, so he moves into the lead job with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson behind him.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 15 to 25 percent of FAAB. Start him as a flex against ATL.

adds.why: Sadiq caught 7 of 8 targets for 105 yards and a touchdown at DET on a season-high 38 snaps with three pass catchers out: Mason Taylor (thumb), Adonai Mitchell (finger) and Omar Cooper Jr. (IR). He ran a route on 58 percent of dropbacks and drew 21.6 percent of the targets, up from a 40 percent route share through Week 2, so Taylor's return is the one thing that caps him.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 12 to 20 percent of FAAB. TE13 for me @CHI, a borderline start this week with Taylor ruled out, if the back lets him play.

adds.why: Allen played all 17 snaps after Breece Hall left at DET and has 19 carries for 61 yards on the year. Isaiah Davis has not taken an offensive snap, so Allen is the back while Hall is week to week.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 8 to 12 percent of FAAB. Flex him @CHI if Hall is out.

adds.why: Allen caught 6 of 9 targets for 63 yards and a touchdown vs HOU with Alec Pierce on IR, and he has 20 targets on 75 routes in three games, 26.7 percent, in a three-man tree that took 30 of 36 attempts. One flag: he faces possible league discipline after a September charge, with a three-game minimum under league policy, none announced, and a court date on Oct 26. The Colts ruled him out of London with the groin on Saturday, so this is a Week 5 claim.
adds.verdict: Claim him, 3 to 6 percent of FAAB. A PPR flex from Week 5 while Pierce is out; he is out for London, so do not play him this week, and monitor the Oct 26 court date.

adds.why: Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and 3 touchdowns at DET, spreading the scores to Garrett Wilson, Sadiq and Jeremy Ruckert. He also took 5 sacks, and Chicago's defense just held PHI to 7 points.
adds.verdict: Stream him @CHI, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB, if your starter is Mayfield or on bye.

adds.why: Higbee caught 8 of 11 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown at DEN once Terrance Ferguson hurt his ankle. Ferguson is ruled out for Week 4, and Colby Parkinson (AC sprain) is questionable, not out, so Parkinson's status decides how many routes Higbee gets.
adds.verdict: Stream him against PHI, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB, and check Parkinson's status at Sunday's inactives.

stashes.why: Harris led the Chargers with 7 targets, 6 catches and 76 yards vs BUF, all career highs, on his smallest snap share of the season: 58 percent after 75 and 82, because Ladd McConkey came back to 88 percent of the snaps and Quentin Johnston played 87. The targets grew while the role shrank.
stashes.verdict: Stash him, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB. He needs a starter to miss time.

stashes.why: Wright held the No. 2 job in camp and was working ahead of Gordon before he sat Week 3 with a stinger and a foot issue. He practiced in full Thursday, is expected to play at MIN and is listed as Miami's RB1, with the staff signaling a shared workload with Gordon.
stashes.verdict: Stash him now, 5 to 10 percent of FAAB. He leads a split backfield Sunday, a bench back until the first-quarter carries show who has the lead role.

stashes.why: Miller is in line for expanded work with Etienne out for an extended stretch, and Kamara has not carried a lead load yet this year.
stashes.verdict: Stash him in 12-team leagues and deeper, 1 to 3 percent of FAAB.

stashes.why: Davis has not taken an offensive snap in three games, but he is the only other back on the Jets roster with Hall hurt and he won camp buzz for the No. 2 job.
stashes.verdict: Stash him in 14-team leagues only, 0 to 1 percent. Bench him until he gets a carry.

drops.why: Torn ACL on his third carry vs KC. He is on IR for the season.
drops.verdict: Drop him unless your league has an open IR slot.

drops.why: One target for 8 yards vs NE on a day Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdowns. He has 13 targets to Parker Washington's 23 through three weeks and no touchdowns.
drops.verdict: Cut him for any of the top six adds above.

drops.why: Worthy ran 19 routes on 24 dropbacks @MIA, a 79 percent route share level with Travis Kelce and one more than Rashee Rice, and drew 2 targets. The routes are there; the production is not: 63 yards on 15 targets in three games with no game above 25.
drops.verdict: Cut him for Sadiq or Keenan Allen.

drops.why: Three carries for minus 4 yards at MIN and 2.1 yards per carry on the season. Bucky Irving out-snapped him 36 to 32, and an undrafted rookie is now at quarterback.
drops.verdict: Cut him for any running back on this list.

mnf.text: Chicago beat Philadelphia 27-7 with Case Keenum at quarterback. D'Andre Swift carried 20 times for 84 yards against his old team. Start Swift as your RB2 vs NYJ.

Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring strain with a three to four week timeline, and Ben Johnson said Tuesday that Tyson Bagent starts vs NYJ if he gets a full week of first-team practice, so first-team reps and the Friday designation decide between Bagent and Case Keenum. Leave Keenum and Bagent on waivers. Hold Rome Odunze; he dropped a wide-open touchdown, which is a better sign than no target at all.
Saquon Barkley ran 15 times for 82 yards, 73 of them in the first half, and Dallas Goedert sat with a knee injury. Start Barkley in Week 4, no change.
